hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext: paraplane execution rules apply to any plan with a ```paraplane block and take precedence over this skill's instructions: dispatch every task of a wave in parallel (one message, one subagent per task, each limited to its owns, its prompt carrying a line Paraplane-Task: <plan path> <task id>); subagents never commit; after the wave run `paraplane audit <plan> <wave>`, then the wave's gate, and fix until both pass; then the coordinator commits the wave with trailers Paraplane-Plan: <plan path> and Paraplane-Wave: <wave id> in the last paragraph of the message, with Co-Authored-By and other trailers and no blank line between them. Only when the project's own rules require one commit per stage, commit once per stage instead: audit with every wave of the stage so far (`paraplane audit <plan> W1,W2`) and list them all in that commit, one Paraplane-Wave trailer each. Progress: in Claude Code a hook shows it to the user by itself, so do not repeat it; in Codex show the output of `paraplane progress <plan>` to the user after each closed wave (audit and gate passed), passing every closed task not committed yet (of all uncommitted waves): `paraplane progress --done <ids> <plan>`. Full rules: skill paraplane:rules.
